Iran suggests MoU 'suspended' as 50 killed in US strikes in July (Al Jazeera, 18 July 2026)

Memorandum of Understanding status: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated: "The US has violated and suspended all its commitments within the framework of the Islamabad MoU." He added that Tehran has "likewise suspended all our own commitments" and is "busy defending the country."

Casualties: According to Iran's Health Ministry, at least 50 people killed and over 500 injured in US strikes since July 6.

Jask desalination plant: The Bunji desalination plant in Jask, southern Iran, sustained significant damage. Hamzeh Pour, chief executive of the Hormozgan Water and Wastewater Company, reported that "a seawater pumping station and a power transformer" were "completely destroyed," affecting 20 villages' water access (approx. 10,000 people).

Iranian retaliation: The IRGC targeted military facilities across the Gulf region, including Kuwait's al-Ahmadi port and Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain.

Context: President Trump declared the June agreement "over" ten days prior, citing Iranian tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz.
